title: K-means, GMM, and EM
summary: Compare hard centroid assignment with probabilistic mixture modeling and use EM as an alternating optimization pattern.
objectives: Describe the E and M steps

sections.title: Lecture core · K-means loop
sections.body: K-means alternates between assigning each point to its nearest centroid and recomputing each centroid from its assigned points. Its objective is a sum of within-cluster squared distances, so scale and outliers matter.

math.explanation: For each data point, choose a cluster index $z_i$ and pay the squared distance to that cluster's centroid. The assignment step lowers the objective by choosing the nearest centroid; the update step lowers it by replacing each centroid with the mean of its assigned points.
math.name: K-means alternating update
math.purpose: Use it to alternate hard assignments and centroid updates while reducing the within-cluster objective.

sections.title: Textbook depth · GMM responsibilities
sections.body: A Gaussian mixture assigns each point a responsibility for every component. Responsibilities are soft: overlapping clusters can both receive meaningful probability, and covariance matrices can represent elongated uncertainty that K-means cannot.

math.explanation: The responsibility is a posterior probability, so the responsibilities for one point sum to one across components. The numerator combines the component prior with the point's likelihood under that component; the denominator normalizes across all components.
math.name: GMM responsibility
math.purpose: Use it to compute the posterior membership weight of a point under each mixture component.

sections.title: Textbook depth · Expectation–maximization
sections.body: The E-step computes responsibilities using the current parameters. The M-step updates weights, means, and covariances using those responsibilities. The observed-data likelihood is improved in the idealized update, but the non-convex objective can still finish at a local optimum.

sections.title: Reference boundary
sections.body: The draft mathematics reference adds a wider clustering and spectral context. Use it to connect ideas after the K-means and EM loop is clear; it is not a replacement for current lecture scope.

examples.title: Worked example: one responsibility update
steps: Suppose a point is equally likely under two components before looking at its location, so both priors are $0.5$.
If the component likelihoods at $x$ are $0.8$ and $0.2$, multiply by the priors to get unnormalized weights $0.4$ and $0.1$.
examples.answer: The E-step normalizes weighted likelihoods; it does not turn the current highest component into permanent ground-truth labeling.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why does a lower K-means objective not prove that the clustering is semantically better?
criticalQuestions.angle: Separate geometric fit under squared distance from the meaning of the labels.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: K-means optimizes within-cluster squared distance. A lower value can reflect scale, outliers, or a chosen $K$ without matching the downstream concept of a useful group.

criticalQuestions.prompt: Why should EM be run from multiple initializations?
criticalQuestions.angle: Connect non-convex likelihood surfaces to local optima.
criticalQuestions.modelAnswer: Different starts can converge to different local solutions. Comparing likelihood, stability, and downstream usefulness is stronger than trusting one run.
